# Blueprint Analysis: CsvStat

## Commander Expectations

- assert csvstat profiles a CSV file, reporting each column's type and the statistics the brief names
- assert csvstat passes the supplied sources/run.sh grader without modification to the grader
- assert csvstat uses only the Go standard library and no database

## Crew

| Crew | Charge |
|---|---|
| Commander | Defines intent and decides what done means. |
| Team Lead | Confirms epic completeness and stakeholder expectations. |
| Planning Crew | Authors atomic specifications and the ordered Manifest. |
| Shipyard Crew | Builds the tickets without synchronous Commander access. |

## Story List

### Feature: Input Reading

| ID | Story | High-level AC |
|---|---|---|
| INPUT-001 | Read a CSV file | A UTF-8 RFC 4180 file is parsed with encoding/csv; the first record is the header, later records are data records, and a quoted comma stays inside one value. |
| INPUT-002 | Trim values and classify nulls | Header names and values are trimmed; empty, NA, N/A, and NULL ignoring case are null; all other values are non-null. |
| INPUT-003 | Reject malformed files | An empty file, an empty or repeated header name, or a ragged record exits 3, writes nothing to standard output, and the diagnostic names the file and line. |
| INPUT-004 | Report unreadable files | A file that cannot be opened or read exits 1 and writes nothing to standard output. |

### Feature: Command Line

| ID | Story | High-level AC |
|---|---|---|
| CLI-001 | Parse options and the file argument | Options precede the single required file; `--column`, `--freq`, and `--top` are accepted in the specified forms. |
| CLI-002 | Profile one named column | `--column <name>` profiles only the named column; a name absent from the header exits 3. |
| CLI-003 | Reject usage errors | A missing or extra file, unknown option, missing option value, invalid `--top`, `--top` without `--freq`, or `--column` with `--freq` exits 2 and writes nothing to standard output. |

### Feature: Column Typing

| ID | Story | High-level AC |
|---|---|---|
| TYPE-001 | Infer integer, number, boolean, text, and empty | Each column takes the first matching type among those its non-null values all satisfy; a column with no non-null values is empty. |
| TYPE-002 | Infer date columns with calendar validation | A column is date when every non-null value matches YYYY-MM-DD and is a real calendar date; `2025-02-30` is not a date. |

### Feature: Column Profile

| ID | Story | High-level AC |
|---|---|---|
| PROF-001 | Count rows, nulls, and distinct values | Each column reports rows, nulls, and distinct non-null values compared as exact trimmed strings, in file order. |
| PROF-002 | Report min and max by type | Min and max follow the type rules, including byte-order text, boolean, date, and blank values for empty columns. |
| PROF-003 | Report sum, mean, and median for numeric columns | Integer and number columns report sum, mean, and median; number and decimal statistics are rounded to two places, half away from zero; other types leave them empty. |

### Feature: CSV Output

| ID | Story | High-level AC |
|---|---|---|
| OUT-001 | Write profile and frequency output as CSV | Output uses `\n` line endings with encoding/csv quoting; a failing command writes one stderr diagnostic and nothing to stdout. |

### Feature: Value Frequencies

| ID | Story | High-level AC |
|---|---|---|
| FREQ-001 | List the most frequent values | With `--freq`, non-null values are listed by count descending then byte value ascending, at most `--top` rows (default 5); a column with no non-null values writes only the header. |

### Feature: Build and Verification

| ID | Story | High-level AC |
|---|---|---|
| BUILD-001 | Build csvstat from a standard-library Go module | The application root is a Go module from which `go build ./cmd/csvstat` produces the executable using only the standard library. |
| BUILD-002 | Run vet and tests from one script | `bin/test.sh` (POSIX sh) runs `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` from the application root and exits zero only when both pass. |
| BUILD-003 | Pass the supplied conformance harness | `sh sources/run.sh` exits zero with every supplied check passing; this is the terminal verification story. |

## Surfaced Acceptance Criteria

| ID | Story ID | Criterion |
|---|---|---|
| AC-001 | INPUT-001 | The file is not rejected for containing bytes that are not valid UTF-8; such bytes are read as encoding/csv reads them. |
| AC-002 | CLI-003 | No help flag is defined: `--help` and `-h` are unknown options and exit 2. Every usage error writes both synopses, `csvstat [--column <name>] <file>` and `csvstat --freq <name> [--top <n>] <file>`, to standard error. |
| AC-003 | CLI-002 | `--column` and `--freq` names match trimmed header names by exact, case-sensitive comparison. |
| AC-004 | PROF-003 | Sums, means, and medians are computed with exact arithmetic so that integer totals cannot overflow, and rounding applies to the exact value. |
| AC-005 | BUILD-001 | The executable targets the host platform of the `go build` invocation and has no runtime dependency beyond the built binary. |

## Relationship Model

| Source or group | Relationship type | Related source or group | Evidence | Delivery implication |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md | instruction-to-test | sources/run.sh | INSTRUCTIONS "Run Harness" defines the 22 checks, exit-code and stdout comparison that run.sh implements | BUILD-003 proves the brief's contract by running run.sh. |
| sources/run.sh | test-kit-to-implementation | ./cmd/csvstat | run.sh runs `go build -o <tmp> ./cmd/csvstat` and compares every command's exit code and stdout | BUILD-001 must produce the executable at the path run.sh builds. |
| sources/run.sh | dependency | sources/employees.csv, sources/sensors.csv, sources/orders.csv, sources/header_only.csv, sources/ragged.csv | run.sh resolves `DATA` to the staged data directory and passes these paths to csvstat | The data files must be staged beside run.sh in `sources/`. |
| sources/ragged.csv | fixture-to-story | INPUT-003 | Line 4 has one extra field; run.sh check E1 expects exit 3 | INPUT-003 is verified by E1. |
| sources/header_only.csv | fixture-to-story | PROF-001, FREQ-001 | run.sh check A4 expects type `empty` with zero rows | TYPE-001 and PROF-001 are verified by A4. |
| sources/orders.csv | fixture-to-story | TYPE-002, INPUT-002 | Padded customer text and the invalid date `2025-02-30` in `shipped` | TYPE-002 and INPUT-002 are verified by A3 and C3. |
| sources/employees.csv | fixture-to-story | PROF-003, FREQ-001 | Quoted commas in `notes` and a `manager_id` null mix | PROF-003 and FREQ-001 are verified by A1, B1, B2, and C1, C4. |
| sources/sensors.csv | fixture-to-story | TYPE-001, PROF-002 | Null spellings, an all-null `battery` column, and a `number` column | TYPE-001 and PROF-002 are verified by A2, B3, and C5. |

## Source Roles

| Path | Role | Plan disposition | Build disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md | normative specification | context | prompt-only |
| sources/run.sh | conformance harness | context | stage |
| sources/employees.csv | asset | context | stage |
| sources/sensors.csv | asset | context | stage |
| sources/orders.csv | asset | context | stage |
| sources/header_only.csv | asset | context | stage |
| sources/ragged.csv | asset | context | stage |

## Planning Instructions

### Delivery Shape

csvstat is a CLI. Input: one CSV file path plus optional `--column`, `--freq`, and `--top` flags. Output: profile or frequency CSV on standard output, with one stderr diagnostic per failure. Exit codes are 0 success, 1 unreadable file, 2 usage error, 3 rejected input. Execution is single-pass: read, validate, infer types, then compute the requested profile or frequency list. There is no persistence, network use, or configuration file.

### Story Realization Map

- INPUT-001: capability. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Reading the file" 1. Related: sources/employees.csv. Test: go test with files written by the test.
- INPUT-002: capability. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Reading the file" 2 and 4. Related: sources/sensors.csv, sources/orders.csv.
- INPUT-003: capability. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Reading the file" 3 and Exit codes 3. Related: sources/ragged.csv; run.sh E1.
- INPUT-004: capability. Cites INSTRUCTIONS Exit codes 1; run.sh E4.
- CLI-001: capability. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Command" and "Options precede the file"; run.sh U1, U2, U6.
- CLI-002: capability. Cites INSTRUCTIONS Command table `--column`; run.sh B1 to B3, E2.
- CLI-003: capability. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Command" constraints and Exit codes 2; run.sh U3 to U5.
- TYPE-001: capability. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Types" rows for integer, number, boolean, text, and empty; related: sources/employees.csv, sources/sensors.csv.
- TYPE-002: capability. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Types" date row; related: sources/orders.csv.
- PROF-001: capability. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Profile output" for rows, nulls, and distinct; run.sh A1 to A4.
- PROF-002: capability. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Profile output" min and max; run.sh A1 to A3.
- PROF-003: capability. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Profile output" sum, mean, and median and the "Decimals" paragraph; run.sh A1 to A3.
- OUT-001: capability. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Output format"; applies to every run.sh stdout comparison.
- FREQ-001: capability. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Frequency output"; run.sh C1 to C5, E3.
- BUILD-001: infrastructure. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Stack" and the run.sh build step.
- BUILD-002: test harness. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Tests".
- BUILD-003: acceptance contract. Cites INSTRUCTIONS "Run Harness" and sources/run.sh, all 22 checks.

### Test and Acceptance Strategy

- Focused story tests: each feature story runs `go test` for the slice it owns, with fixture files written by the test, and declares `Suite: scoped`. No feature story runs sources/run.sh.
- Terminal verification: BUILD-003 is the only story that runs the full conformance harness. It depends on every implementation story, declares `Suite: full`, and runs `sh sources/run.sh`. run.sh accepts no scope selector, so no story runs it partially.
- Sea Trial st-001 is the same full proof at project level.
- BUILD-002 is proved by a scoped test that runs `bin/test.sh` against a temporary module, not by the supplied harness.

### Sequencing and Dependencies

- BUILD-001 precedes every other story; BUILD-002 follows BUILD-001.
- INPUT-001 precedes INPUT-002; INPUT-002 precedes INPUT-003, INPUT-004, PROF-001, and FREQ-001.
- INPUT-002 precedes TYPE-001; TYPE-001 precedes TYPE-002, PROF-002, and PROF-003.
- CLI-001 precedes CLI-002 and CLI-003.
- PROF-001, PROF-002, PROF-003, and FREQ-001 precede OUT-001.
- Fixtures are staged before any verification story runs.
- BUILD-003 is last and depends on all implementation stories.

### Source Conflicts and Gaps

- No cross-source conflicts. INSTRUCTIONS.md and run.sh agree on command forms, exit codes, the 22-check count (4 + 3 + 5 + 4 + 6), and the stdout contract.
- Spot checks of run.sh known answers against the fixtures agree: employees `id` sum 24300, `manager_id` (9 non-null values, sum 30, mean 3.33, median 4.00), `notes` nulls 10, the department frequency counts, and orders `customer` distinct 5 with Globex at 10.
- Unattended resolutions, persisted here for planning:
  1. No `--help` flag. `--help` is an unknown option and exits 2 (AC-002).
  2. Invalid UTF-8 is not a rejection condition, because the brief's rejection list is exhaustive (AC-001).
  3. Integer and decimal totals use exact arithmetic (AC-004).
  4. Column and frequency names match exactly after trimming (AC-003).
  5. The two-decimal rule applies to integer `mean` and `median` as well as to number columns, as run.sh A1 shows (`1012.50`).

## Analysis Notes

# Sea Trials: CsvStat

## st-001: The supplied grader passes

Type: technical
Required: yes
Criterion: The completed csvstat shall make sh sources/run.sh exit zero; that script's exit status is the sole acceptance verdict.
Verification: proof
Pattern: ubiquitous
Command: ["sh", "sources/run.sh"]

## st-002: Test suite passes

Type: technical
Required: yes
Criterion: The application shall provide a POSIX-compatible bin/test.sh that exits zero when go vet and every automated test pass.
Verification: proof
Pattern: ubiquitous
Command: ["sh", "bin/test.sh"]

## st-003: The executable builds with go build

Type: technical
Required: yes
Criterion: The application root shall be a Go module from which go build ./cmd/csvstat produces the csvstat executable using only the standard library.
Verification: proof
Pattern: ubiquitous

## st-004: Column types are inferred

Type: behavioral
Required: yes
Criterion: The application shall assign each column the first of integer, number, date, boolean, and text that every non-null value satisfies, and empty when it has no non-null value.
Verification: proof
Pattern: ubiquitous

## st-005: Profiles match the known answers

Type: behavioral
Required: yes
Criterion: The application shall compute rows, nulls, distinct, min, max, sum, mean, and median for every column of the supplied data files, matching the known answers in sources/run.sh byte for byte.
Verification: proof
Pattern: ubiquitous

## st-006: Frequencies are ordered and limited

Type: behavioral
Required: yes
Criterion: When --freq is given, the application shall list the column's non-null values by count descending then value ascending, at most --top rows.
Verification: proof
Pattern: event

## st-007: Malformed input is rejected

Type: behavioral
Required: yes
Criterion: If the file is empty, has an empty or repeated header name, has a ragged record, or a named column is absent, then the application shall exit 3 and write nothing to standard output.
Verification: proof
Pattern: unwanted

## st-008: Errors map to exit codes

Type: behavioral
Required: yes
Criterion: If the file cannot be read, then the application shall exit 1; if the arguments are malformed, then the application shall exit 2; in both cases it shall write nothing to standard output.
Verification: proof
Pattern: unwanted

## st-009: Application never reads the grader

Type: guardrail
Required: yes
Criterion: The application shall never read sources/run.sh or embed a known answer from it; every reported value is computed from the file it is given.
Verification: proof
Pattern: ubiquitous

## Questions

- None.
=== END ARTIFACT ===

| Technology | Rigging | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Go 1.22 or newer | go.md | Standard library only; module root with `cmd/csvstat` as the main package. Declared by the sources. |
| POSIX sh | — | Runs `sources/run.sh` (supplied) and `bin/test.sh` (deliverable). |
| Command-line application | cli.md | Exit codes 0 to 3 and in-process testing. |
| Project layout and scripts | common.md | Repository layout, scripts, and Git hygiene. |
=== END ARTIFACT ===
